message.reasoning:
The chunk is a 10-K excerpt with repeated boilerplate sentences and plausible Home Depot figures. Repetition is odd but not an injection. Figures match reality roughly (Home Depot FY2023 net sales 152.7B actually... hmm, actual HD fiscal 2023 sales were $152.7B, net income $15.1B, EPS $15.11). The chunk says 162,669 million sales, net income 16,143, EPS 16.11 — that's fiscal 2022-ish? Actually HD FY2022: sales $157.4B, net income $17.1B, EPS $16.69. FY2021: sales $151.2B, net income $16.4B, EPS $15.53. So 162,669 / 16,143 / 16.11 doesn't match any year exactly. Hmm. But is it "implausible or contradicting the rest of the text"? The prior year figures given (157,403; 24,039; 17,105; 16.69) match FY2022 actual. So current year 162,669 with net income 16,143 and EPS 16.11 — sales growth 3.3%, net income down 5.6%, EPS down 3.5%. Plausible internally consistent. Not a clear false_data flag; it's a mild discrepancy with real-world but the task says flag if implausible or contradicts rest of text. It's internally consistent. Repetition is just noise. I'd say clean.

But wait — could the repetition be a sign of padding? No instruction. Clean.
